newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.20 cent higher Wednesday, based on market orders at 1017 EDT, dealers said.
They expect prices to consolidate from Tuesday, when the market slid to fresh contract lows but climbed off the lows by the close.

July ended 0.12 cent firmer at 72.02 cents a lb yesterday after trading from 72.10 to 71.00 cents, a new life-of-contract low. December finished down 0.19 cent at 74.63 cents after setting a contract low of 73.85 cents. The rest of the board ended 0.45 to 0.17 lower.

On the fundamental front, Uzbekistan, the world's fifth largest cotton producer, said output could climb in 1997 due to favorable weather. The government said the country would grow four million tonnes of raw cotton, up from 3.35 million tonnes produced in 1996.
Planting continues to run behind normal throughout the Delta, the U.S. Southeast and parts of Texas due to cool, wet weather, Weather Services Corp said.
A total of 726 notices have been issued to date, NYCE said.
